implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.py defines BOARD_SIZE = 15; Board.__init__ creates a grid of size BOARD_SIZE x BOARD_SIZE.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players (black and white) alternate turns
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameController.__init__ sets current_player = BLACK; GameController.switch_turn toggles between BLACK and WHITE after each valid move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Place stones on empty intersections only
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_move checks bounds and EMPTY; Board.place_stone uses this check before writing the player value.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a win of five stones horizontally
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win iterates over direction (0,1) and counts consecutive stones; returns cells when count >= 5.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a win of five stones vertically
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win includes direction (1,0) for vertical scanning.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a win of five stones on both diagonals
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win includes directions (1,1) and (1,-1) for diagonal scanning.
Board.is_full returns True when no EMPTY cells remain; GameController.handle_click sets game_over and status_text to MSG_DRAW when is_full() is true.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graphical UI with pygame showing board, stones, last‑move highlight, win highlight, hover preview, and status bar
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py implements drawing of grid, stones, last move (COLOR_LAST_MOVE), winning line (COLOR_WIN), hover preview, and status bar; main.py runs the pygame loop.
main.py catches ImportError in run_gui and calls run_console(), which uses Board and simple text rendering.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ability to restart the game after a win or draw
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameController.reset clears board and resets state; main loop listens for 'R' key and calls controller.reset().

judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable Gomoku implementation. The board size, turn logic, move validation, win detection (horizontal, vertical, both diagonals), draw detection, GUI rendering, hover preview, and console fallback are all present and backed by concrete code. No major missing functionality or fatal bugs were found, so the submission meets the benchmark requirements.
